main_body: A flat 4x3-tile ground patch of dark gothic mossy flagstone/cobble with small tufts and reddish specks, filling the whole 64x48 canvas. It is terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none - flat ground texture with no standing top/front structure; the column scan shows only a repeating 16-row pattern of dark greens (L~50) with a lighter 2-row line (L~76) and a dark 1-row line.
evidence: Terrain tile patch: the contract for standing objects does not apply. The ground repeats seamlessly with no object volume, no top/front split and no receding side faces. Nothing in it reads as a wrongly drawn standing object, so it passes Part A as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours in total and a median of 6 per tile, against 80 colours and a median of 26 for the grass reference. It has about 3 lightness steps of dark green, plus a few reddish dots. The texture is a regular repeating tuft pattern of small mounds with dark shadow bars, which reads as tiled and mechanical rather than hand-shaded. The 0% flat-fill coverage is because of the repetition, not richness. Dark edge pixels are tinted (2% neutral), so the outline is fine. The paving reference also has 7 colours per tile, but it carries stone-by-stone shading and clear structure, while the candidate is murky and low in contrast, with very little value separation. Next to the grass reference it looks much thinner, so it fails.
